sources_considered.why: Full-text representative survey measures adoption, awareness of platforms, and personal versus business use. It does not measure token-cost awareness, training, or net benefits.
Full-text study reports consumer valuations from July 2025 and March 2026. It offers relevant alternative evidence about benefits but does not measure the claimed May population or causal mechanism.
Full-text original abstract provides technical context about token consumption without substituting model behavior for evidence about users.
Read in full, but selected-company reporting cannot establish an overwhelming majority of all AI users.

evidence_items.explanation: The study finds variable token consumption and a weak relationship between greater consumption and accuracy in coding tasks. It does not measure users' cost awareness, training, population prevalence, or economic benefits, and predates the target month.

unresolved_gaps: No representative May study jointly measures cost awareness and deliberate incentives to ignore costs.
No matching population estimate establishes an overwhelming majority.
No study links those variables causally to costs exceeding benefits.
The statement does not identify whose costs and benefits determine whether use is economical.
